idea.title: A passing build is not the same as a releasable image
idea.summary: A production dependency vulnerability was removed with a scoped override, then the exact candidate SHA was verified through CI, image scanning, immutable revision checks, and runtime health checks before any promotion.

context.goal: Verify a dependency remediation without promoting or deploying it.
context.situation: The previous candidate image had one actionable HIGH finding in a transitive Prisma operational dependency.
context.problem: An application test pass alone could not establish that the release image was secure or bootable.
context.investigation: The dependency chain and image build were traced, then the exact candidate SHA was run through CI and candidate-only image verification.
context.decision: Keep the candidate isolated from production and require immutable image, Trivy, revision, and health evidence.
context.implementation: Used the existing manual candidate CI and image workflows with an exact SHA.
context.result: CI, Trivy, image revision, startup, health, and readiness checks passed without a production status or deployment.

learning_points: A dependency fix needs verification in the production image, not only in the package manager lockfile.
Candidate registries and immutable revisions let teams verify a release without promoting it.
Operational tooling such as Prisma can be a production image dependency even when request handlers do not import it.
story_points: One transitive HIGH finding blocked an otherwise passing candidate.
The remediation stayed scoped to the dependency resolution.
The release remained isolated while verification gates ran.
possible_angles: Why CI green is not enough for a container release.
The overlooked runtime dependency: operational tooling inside the image.
How immutable candidate images reduce promotion risk.

notes: No customer data, credentials, or private logs were captured.
